# Assurly

> A pre-deploy ship gate for AI-built SaaS. Scan a deployed URL or a Next.js + Supabase + Stripe + Vercel codebase and get one verdict — ship or don't — before it reaches production.

Assurly exists for people who build fast with AI tools (Lovable, v0, Bolt, Cursor, Replit) and are not security specialists. Those tools produce working code quickly but routinely leave the production wiring unfinished: a database table without row-level security, a payment webhook that never verifies its signature, a service key that ships to the browser.

It answers one question — "can I ship this right now?" — with a Ship Score out of 100 and one of three verdicts: READY TO SHIP, REVIEW RECOMMENDED, or NOT READY TO SHIP. Findings come with the exact fix (the SQL statement, the config change), not just a warning.

Source code is analysed locally by the CLI and never uploaded. The hosted product additionally probes a live URL and can open fix pull requests.

## Packages

- [assurly](https://www.npmjs.com/package/assurly): the CLI. `npx assurly scan --path .` runs the gate locally, exits non-zero when blocked, so it drops into CI.
- [@assurly/mcp-server](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@assurly/mcp-server): the same gate over the Model Context Protocol, so an AI agent in Cursor or Claude Code can check its own work before shipping.
- [@assurly/scanner-core](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@assurly/scanner-core): the rules on their own, for building other tooling. Runs in Node or the browser.

## What it checks

Supabase row-level security gaps and exposed service-role keys; Stripe webhook signature verification; secrets and undocumented environment variables reaching the client bundle; React Server Component data leaks; SQL and migration safety; serverless connection pooling; Vercel edge compatibility; cold-start cost; TypeScript strictness; and missing CI checks.
